6S Success: Home Quest

Rewritten six-page master plan plus a whole-home card appendix. The system converts the current Entryway prototype into configurable micro-zone mini decks that can be pulled, selected, assigned, or app-generated into 15–90 minute cooperative quests, Escape Quests, Boss Battles, and Home Raids.

PAGE 1 OF 6

Product Architecture: The Home Becomes the Game Board

Home Quest is no longer designed as a single fixed deck per room. Each room is a collection of micro-zone mini decks. Players build only the parts that exist in their home and use those cards to generate real improvement events.

HOME → ROOM → MICRO ZONE → 6S ACTION → PROBLEM → COUNTERMEASURE → HABIT → VALIDATION → WIN
Core product rule: every quest must leave behind an improved system. A cleaner area is not enough. Players should be able to find items faster, return them more easily, see the correct condition, identify hazards, and maintain the result.

Each Micro-Zone Mini Deck

Every significant micro zone receives a standard 12-card mini deck: 1 Micro Zone anchor, 6 core 6S action cards, 1 Problem, 1 Tool, 1 Habit, 1 Upgrade, and 1 Win/Reward. Room cards and room-level Event cards sit above those mini decks.

Mini-deck componentCountPurpose
Micro Zone1Defines function, scope, and the zone-level quest.
6S Actions6Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain.
Problem1Recognizable failure mode that can trigger a quest or Boss Battle.
Tool1Physical, visual, digital, improvised, purchased, or 3D-printed countermeasure.
Habit1Small repeatable behavior that prevents regression.
Upgrade1Improvement after the basic system works.
Win / Reward1Validated household outcome, not just points.
PAGE 2 OF 6

Quest Generation: 15–90 Minutes, Multiple Entry Points

Players should be able to begin with the problem they feel, the time they have, the room they want to improve, the 6S skill they want to practice, or simply a desire for a random challenge.

By Micro Zone
“Give us a 30-minute bathroom vanity quest.”
By 6S
“Give us a 30-minute Sort event across the house.”
By Problem
“The laundry mountain is out of control.”
Random Pull
Shuffle eligible cards and let the system choose.
Assigned
A parent, partner, roommate, coach, or facilitator assigns cards.
Self-Selected
Players voluntarily build a quest around what matters most.

Standard Time Boxes

ModeTimeTypical Scope
Quick Win15 minOne obvious problem or one 6S action.
Mini Quest20 minSmall micro zone.
Power Reset30 minMeaningful micro zone or 2–3 targeted cards.
Focused Event45 minFull 6S on a small/medium zone.
6S Event60 minMajor zone, several zones, or team play.
Room Kaizen / Raid90 minMulti-zone transformation plus final audit.

Cards therefore need metadata for Room, Micro Zone, 6S, expected time, difficulty, players, completion test, countermeasure, Sustain behavior, and supported quest modes. Those fields are built into the appendix.

PAGE 3 OF 6

Cooperative Play: Make Group Quests Feel Like an Escape Room

Group play should emphasize simultaneous action, hidden information, role ownership, interruptions, and a final proof that the new system works. Avoid having six people stand around one drawer.

Recommended Group Roles

Sorter
Owns remove / keep / move decisions.
Organizer
Owns Straighten and point-of-use placement.
Inspector
Owns Shine and Safety findings.
Standardizer
Owns labels, limits, visual controls, and checklists.
Runner
Moves items between rooms and handles exit flow.
Auditor
Tests someone else's finished zone and can reject weak completion.

Quest Chain

MISSION REVEALED → ROLES → TIMER → PARALLEL ACTIONS → UNLOCK → CHAOS EVENT → COUNTERMEASURE → FINAL AUDIT → ESCAPE

Micro-zone cards can be physically hidden at the location they should belong, placed in sealed envelopes, or digitally gated in the app. Completing one card may reveal another. A Problem card may become a Boss with “health” removed by completing 6S actions. Event cards can interrupt the team with Surprise Visitors, Missing Item Tests, Time Attacks, or Role-Swap Audits.

Escape condition: success should be observable. Another player can find the keys, identify the pantry categories, retrieve five garage tools, load the dishwasher correctly, or restore the room within a set time.
PAGE 4 OF 6

Card System: Existing Entryway + New Mini-Deck Standard

The current 90-card Entryway deck remains valuable and is preserved verbatim in the appendix as the canonical prototype. It contains Room, Micro Zone, Problem, Tool, Habit, Skill, Upgrade, Win/Reward, and Event families. The new architecture does not discard it. It maps those ideas into a scalable micro-zone system.

What Changes

  • Skills become Universal Core cards rather than being unnecessarily duplicated in every room.
  • Every micro zone gets its own six 6S actions, so users can filter and pull by activity.
  • Problems trigger quests and Boss Battles instead of merely acting as penalties.
  • Tools become countermeasures that can be owned, improvised, bought, or 3D printed.
  • Habits become Sustain contracts tied to specific zones.
  • Wins require proof through a find/return/reset/user test.
  • Events become stress tests that make the house “fight back.”

Universal Core Skills

Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain, Visual Control, Point of Use, Reduce Motion, Simplify, Continuous Improvement, and Quick Win become reusable powers across all rooms.

Production Order

  1. Confirm the room mission and micro-zone map.
  2. Validate that every micro zone represents a real household function.
  3. Write the six zone-specific 6S actions.
  4. Define the most recognizable failure mode.
  5. Choose the simplest countermeasure/tool.
  6. Define one Sustain habit and one post-reset Upgrade.
  7. Define a Win that can be objectively tested.
  8. Tag time, difficulty, players, and compatible quest modes.
  9. Build room-level Events and Escape conditions.
  10. Only then create card art.
PAGE 6 OF 6

Digital + Physical Ecosystem and Final Gameplay Loop

The app should operate as Game Master while the physical home remains the board. It can generate quests from the appendix metadata, time stages, reveal cards, distribute hidden objectives, validate codes or photos, call random tests, and record Before/After results.

PICK TIME → PICK SCOPE → PULL / SELECT / ASSIGN → RUN CLOCK → COMPLETE CARDS → INSTALL COUNTERMEASURES → FINAL TEST → SET STANDARD → ASSIGN HABIT → EARN WIN

Physical/Digital Bridge

  • QR on each Micro Zone card opens that exact zone in the app.
  • Photo audit can recommend eligible cards.
  • UPC scans can establish consumable min/max and reorder triggers.
  • Tool cards can link to owned items, shopping, or Gridfinity/3D-print solutions.
  • Players can save custom home decks containing only the zones they actually have.
  • Family and group quests can divide work across roles and rooms, then converge for a final audit.
Defining promise: your real home is the board, real household friction is the puzzle, 6S is the power system, the cards generate the mission, and winning leaves the household objectively easier to live in.
